about: Every engine, model, tool and provider Regista can use: the single source for scripts/install.sh, scripts/doctor.sh,
the app (RegistaCore EngineManifest, engines.status) and docs/reference/engines.md (scripts/reference-docs.sh).
Download facts (version, release and pin dates, sha256, download size, url) live ONLY in scripts/engines.lock:
an entry names its lock rows in 'artifacts' (an id ending with ':' means every row with that prefix).
minRamGB is the minimum RAM; the tier (base/medium/pro) is derived from it with 'tiers'. null = planned.
diskBytes = installed footprint, measured with du on the owner's Mac (M5 Pro, 2026-11-12) where it differs from the
download; when absent the footprint is the sum of the artifacts' download sizes; null = unknown.
install.method: installer (scripts/install.sh step), homebrew, system (macOS), firstUse (downloaded by the engine
the first time it is needed), manual (steps), cloud. status: available (Regista uses it) or planned (not built).
files: what the engine puts in Regista's engines folder (~/Library/Application Support/Regista/engines), relative to it:
the Motori screen removes exactly these, and scripts/install.sh --only <id> downloads a single-artifact entry to its one file.
scripts: the small helper files the installer copies from the repository's engines/ (never a lock file, an environment or a
model): the app replaces those of an installed engine that differ from its own copy, at launch and when the engine is used.
shipped: on the entries a release build ships inside the app (#107), the shipped build's licence and size in bytes (the
binary in Contents/Helpers, from scripts/build-engines.sh's BUILD-INFO.txt): Settings › Engines and engines.status show
these for a shipped engine, not the installable one's (#114).
After editing: scripts/reference-docs.sh (regenerates docs/reference/engines.md; the pre-commit hook runs --check).
tierDetectNote: detectFromGB sits below the nominal size: macOS reports slightly less than 16/32 GiB on some models.
diskMarginNote: headroom for the install itself: the 1.6 GB source of the faster-whisper conversion (deleted afterwards), the download cache and logs

engines.name: ComfyUI
engines.role: local generation server (comfy-gen CLI and workflow runner)
unlocks: local images, clips, music and upscale (free)

steps: Install ComfyUI by following its own instructions (https://docs.comfy.org), in a Python environment of its own, and put the model files generate.check lists in ComfyUI's models folders (Regista's workflows name each file exactly).

Put the comfy-gen command (images and clips) in ~/.local/bin, or set comfyGen in engines.json to where it is; for music and upscale, set comfyRun in engines.json to the comfy_run.py runner. Both read their ComfyUI workflows from a workflows folder beside them.
Check it: ask Claude for generate.check (or run scripts/install.sh --with comfyui). It lists every missing node pack and model file, with the ComfyUI folder it goes in.

engines.notes: diskBytes = the clone with its venv
